headline: India's Ringg secures $10M from Peak XV to expand voice AI services
summary: The voice AI startup, processing 20 million calls monthly, extends its Series A to $15.5 million total, targeting complex enterprise workflows in India and beyond.
details: Ringg, an Indian voice AI startup, has landed $10 million from Peak XV Partners as an extension of its Series A. This brings the round's total to $15.5 million, following an initial $5.5 million raised earlier this year.

The company currently processes 20 million call attempts each month. This growth is fueled by India's strong preference for phone calls, with over 76% of consumers favoring voice communication with businesses.

Initially a text-to-speech startup called DesiVocal, Ringg pivoted to building voice AI agents for enterprises. Its first customer was Indian fintech Cred, and it now serves major Indian startups including Flipkart, Practo, Groww, and PolicyBazaar.

Ringg has evolved beyond high-volume, low-complexity use cases like outbound calling and lead qualification. It now focuses on more intricate workflows such as appointment booking for healthcare, abandoned-cart recovery for e-commerce, and onboarding/KYC checks for fintech apps.

While voice calls still constitute over 70% of Ringg's business, the startup is expanding into other channels like chat and WhatsApp. It also automates browser-based support requests for clients such as Shell, aiming to be a platform for agents that deliver outcomes.

The company develops its own speech recognition and generation models, with aspirations to own the full voice stack, including infrastructure and deployment. Currently, its product functions as an orchestration layer, routing tasks to various models based on the use case.

Peak XV principal Rishen Kapoor highlights Ringg's technical depth, stemming from its origins as a research lab. This capability allows them to tackle challenging enterprise workflows end-to-end, completing high-value tasks with consistent quality.

Ringg operates in a competitive Indian voice AI market, alongside model makers like Deepgram and local players such as Sarvam, as well as orchestration-focused startups like Bolna. The company's strategy focuses on owning customer relationships and delivering tangible outcomes.

Ringg currently employs 40 people, with over 15 hires in the last three months. The startup is actively recruiting for forward-deployed engineer roles and researchers to further reduce the cost of running its advanced AI models.
